item.content:encoded:
Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa, appeared on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan.

The show focused on the state of preparedness of the Fijian Elections Office for the proposed national referendum on December 9th and the next general elections which has to be held by February 6th 2027, the nationwide voter registration underway, changes to the electoral laws and the impact on the voters and the country, and the impact of any drastic changes with two months to go for the last day for the Writ of Elections to be issued on December 24th 2026 amongst other issues.

Watch the Straight Talk interview on our facebook page, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram accounts.

You can also check out the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple podcasts.

item.title: Landowners must be consulted on constitutional changes affecting their land rights
item.description: iTaukei landowners must be properly informed and consulted before development projects proceed, with concerns raised over how the proposed constitutional amendments will protect customary land rights and ensure land remains available for future generations. This was raised by 20-year-old Laite Masitabua of Nasekula, Macuata, while speaking before the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Con
item.content:encoded:
iTaukei landowners must be properly informed and consulted before development projects proceed, with concerns raised over how the proposed constitutional amendments will protect customary land rights and ensure land remains available for future generations.

This was raised by 20-year-old Laite Masitabua of Nasekula, Macuata, while speaking before the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill at the Suva Civic Centre.

Masitabua questioned how the proposed changes relating to consultation on land and resources would ensure affected landowners are properly informed, meaningfully consulted and given the opportunity to express their concerns before development projects proceed.

She also asked what practical improvements the proposed Section 48 of the Constitution Amendment Bill would bring to the protection of customary land ownership rights, compared with Section 28 of the current 2013 Constitution.

Masitabua says land is not just an economic resource, but is also part of the identity of iTaukei people, their habitat and something they rely on.

She questioned how people living in villages would be informed about the proposed constitutional amendments, particularly when development projects could affect their land and resources.

She asked whether the Government would arrange meetings with landowners in their villages to explain the proposed changes and allow them to discuss their concerns.

Masitabua also raised concerns about young people who move to towns for education and other opportunities, saying some end up homeless despite having land back in their villages.

She questioned why iTaukei landowners cannot lease their own land.

Insert: Masitabua on land issues 19th Oct 26

She says land belongs to the people and must be protected for future generations, stressing that decisions involving customary land must take into account the rights and interests of those who will inherit it.

item.title: Differing opinions on Constitution Amendment Bill are healthy – Tikoduadua
item.description: Minister for Defence and Veteran Affairs Pio Tikoduadua says people have differing views on the Constitution Amendment Bill, and such discussions are healthy before Parliament makes a final decision. When asked whether he supports concerns raised about the fast-tracking of the constitutional amendment process, Tikoduadua says people are entitled to their own opinions.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Defence and Veteran Affairs Pio Tikoduadua says people have differing views on the Constitution Amendment Bill, and such discussions are healthy before Parliament makes a final decision.

When asked whether he supports concerns raised about the fast-tracking of the constitutional amendment process, Tikoduadua says people are entitled to their own opinions.

He says the proposed constitutional changes remain open for national discussion until Parliament makes a decision.

Tikoduadua says people should be allowed to share their views during the consultation process, as many useful ideas are being raised.

He adds that some people are trying to get ahead of the process, and it is important to allow discussions to continue within the time available.

On the proposed immunity provisions, Tikoduadua says he has been having discussions with the RFMF Commander and the military institution about their views.

He says the RFMF's position is already public, and its contribution is important given its role in Fiji's national security.

Tikoduadua stresses that constitutional reform is a national issue, and people should listen to one another.

When questioned about differences within the coalition government over the proposed amendments, Tikoduadua says the coalition remains united.

He says differing opinions among coalition partners should not be seen as a sign of division, but as part of healthy discussions aimed at producing the best Constitution for Fiji and its people.

item.title: El Niño effects continue to intensify in Lautoka as students and farmers suffer
item.description: The effects of El Niño continue to intensify, with Lautoka residents saying the water situation has worsened over the past four to five months, leaving some communities without water for days and affecting students preparing for their exams. Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka Residents and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says the situation has worsened, affecting students who are
item.content:encoded:
The effects of El Niño continue to intensify, with Lautoka residents saying the water situation has worsened over the past four to five months, leaving some communities without water for days and affecting students preparing for their exams.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka Residents and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says the situation has worsened, affecting students who are preparing for their examinations.

Reddy says some students have reported wearing the same school uniform for two to three days because they do not have enough water to wash their clothes.

Insert:Reddy on affected students 21st Oct

He says residents in interior parts of Lautoka, including Tavakubu and Saru, are experiencing water shortages, with some going without supply for three to four days.

Reddy says the river that many residents rely on for water has also dried up, making life even more difficult for affected communities.

He says the supply of vegetables has also decreased due to El Niño, resulting in a significant increase in prices.

Meanwhile, Reddy says livestock farmers have been forced to sell many of their goats and cows because of the lack of water, while some animals are dying.

He is calling on the Government to provide water to communities in Lautoka that are experiencing shortages.
